author: Master Elric Varn, tutor in the arcane
pages:
#On Magicka

Every living creature carries within it a measure of magicka, a well of power that spells draw upon. Cast a spell and the well empties a little. Rest and it refills. Those who train their minds can deepen the well over the years.

Do not cast when the well is dry. You will not die, but you will feel very foolish, waving your hands at an angry bandit with nothing happening.

#The Five Schools

Destruction is the art of harm: fire, frost and lightning flung from the hands.

Restoration heals wounds, wards away hostile spells and turns back the restless dead.

Alteration changes the world: it hardens skin, lights the dark and lets you breathe underwater.

Conjuration calls servants from beyond and binds weapons of pure energy.

Illusion works upon the mind: it calms, frightens, enrages or conceals.

#Learning New Spells

Spells are learned from tomes. Reading a tome burns its knowledge into your mind and consumes the book, so do not buy the same one twice. Court mages and the shops of wizards sell them; old ruins sometimes hold them.

Practice a school and you will grow better at it. Spells will cost less, last longer and strike harder.

#A Word on Safety

Do not practise fire spells indoors. Do not practise frost spells near the well. Do not practise conjuration at all until someone experienced is standing next to you. And do not, under any circumstances, attempt to calm a dragon.
